In the blink of an eye, it’s the last day of the year again.

In 2021 the account published 25 articles and gained two new authors. Since our first article on July 7, 2019, we have published 81 original articles and shared or edited 8 videos. On October 24 this year our following reached five figures. We now have 10,630 followers, and the largest group is aged 26–35, at 46%.

It has been exactly three years since I started writing popular-science articles and answers on Zhihu at the end of 2018. Only once I started putting things out there did I slowly realize how little I really knew. After a few pieces on subjects I knew well, every new piece meant learning something new. I’ve learned a lot in these three years, and I’m even more grateful to have met the friends in our authors’ group and so many fellow acousticians. Writing hasn’t always been smooth sailing. Squeeze a little harder and more milk will come out? Not always. Sometimes, picking a topic or trying to make a piece more fun to read, Er Mu and I were tearing our hair out. Still, two people working together generate more drive than one. As far as I remember, we slipped only twice and missed our every-two-weeks schedule, so we’re fairly pleased with our “self-discipline.”

Along the way, some followers left messages saying they had chosen acoustics because of us. At moments like that I feel that this thing the two of us cooked up really means something, and our motivation goes straight to max. At the same time, I hope we haven’t led anyone astray, haha. But I do have to say this: what appears on the account is, after all, the personal take of the two of us and a handful of authors. Like all popular science, it presents knowledge as we ourselves have understood it, which means some bias is inevitable, as are mistakes we haven’t noticed. So, readers, consider yourselves warned: for rigorous knowledge, go to the professional books and literature. Whether on Zhihu or on WeChat, the point of popular-science articles is to introduce more people to a field. For digging deep into one, this is not the best place.

I forget whether it was this year or last, but our goal was to keep the account going until the end of 2021. We did it. Woohoo! Er Mu and I both like taking things on, and over these two-plus years we’ve poured countless hours of our free time into running the account. We feel it’s time to go and take on something else, even though we haven’t worked out exactly what. That doesn’t mean the account is going quiet. We just won’t stick to a strict schedule of one article every two weeks anymore. When something comes up that we want to write about, or we see a fun video, we’ll still post it here. As we go deeper into our own work, I’m sure we’ll have new things to share. Fellow acousticians who enjoy writing are still welcome to come and write about whatever you’d like. Ziyu Acoustics will always be here, and anyone who wants to reach us can still send us a message through the account.

In 2022 my own life will change in a few ways, and I’m quite looking forward to it. I hope both life and work move in the directions I want. Thank you, readers, for following us all this time, and thank you to the members of our authors’ group for everything you’ve contributed. Without you we wouldn’t have come this far. Finally, I hope all of you who follow the account reach your goals, big and small, in 2022. Happy New Year!
